title: What Do Financial Officers Predict for the Labor Market? - San Francisco Fed
gist: SF Fed shows CFO Survey wage expectations track realized US wage growth since 2002 better than household surveys (RMSE 0.69pp); 2026 expectations of 4% wages imply only ~0.4pp real wage growth and moderating employment growth of 2.4%.

themes.theme: CFO wage expectations as a signal

insights.claim: CFO Survey wage growth expectations tracked realized US wage growth since 2002 with a root mean-squared forecast error of 0.69 percentage point and beat both NY Fed SCE and Michigan household survey expectations in all periods tested.
insights.speaker: Stephie Fried
insights.so_what: Employer surveys are a better wage-growth indicator than household expectations.

insights.claim: CFO expectations and realized wages both averaged about 3% in 2002-2019, but in 2020-2025 realized growth averaged 4.4% versus 5.2% expected, with CFOs overpredicting after 2022.
insights.speaker: Stephie Fried

insights.claim: CFO wage growth expectations for 2026 are 4%, well below the 7.0% peak for 2022, while realized wage growth fell from 5.5% in 2022 to 3.0% in 2025.
insights.speaker: Stephie Fried

insights.claim: Real wage growth fell to just 0.1pp in 2025, and the authors forecast 0.4pp for 2026 (4% wages less 3.6% expected PCE inflation), implying weak purchasing-power gains at best.
insights.speaker: Stephie Fried
insights.so_what: Squeezed real incomes are a consumer-spending risk.

insights.claim: Wage expectations should not be read as price-inflation forecasts, since wage-price links depend on productivity, margins and conditions.
insights.speaker: Stephie Fried
insights.so_what: Do not map wage signals directly to inflation.

insights.claim: CFOs expect 2.4% full-time employment growth for 2026, below ~3.5% for 2024-25 but above the 1.8% 2002-25 average, suggesting a roughly balanced labor market.
insights.speaker: Stephie Fried
insights.so_what: Moderating labor demand without a collapse.

insights.claim: Since 2022 CFOs expected 3.9% employment growth versus realized 0.9% full-time and 1.4% private payroll growth, so employment expectations have run persistently too high.
insights.speaker: Stephie Fried
insights.so_what: Discount CFO hiring intentions; they overpredict.

top_entities: Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco
